keep.title: Pausing the dispatcher does not freeze custody: release()/rescueERC20() are not whenNotPaused, so held USDC can still leave during a pause
keep.ledgerReconciliation: No fingerprint match in ledger → origin: new. Adjacent to OPEN L-04 (49fb985f… 'privileged mintFor()/burn() ignore paused flags' on NFTMinterV2) — same 'privileged path ignores pause' family but distinct contract/function/impact (value-MINTING bypass vs custody-freeze-expectation gap on the new story-043 dispatcher). Cross-reference only; DO NOT merge (distinct fingerprint).
keep.knownIssueCheck: NOT covered by any of the 7 known issues. KI-4 (owner trust for pausing) and KI-5 (pauser trust) grant trust for the pause/unpause ACTION itself; they do NOT bless the non-obvious SEMANTIC gap that pausing halts only the inbound mint/debt side while a whitelisted releaser keeps moving held USDC mid-pause. This is the Law-3 footgun exception: a competent non-malicious owner would be surprised that pause does not freeze custody ⇒ in scope as an operational hazard. (rescueERC20 being un-gated is intended escape-hatch and correct; the release() releaser path is the reportable substance.)
keep.lawNote: Law-3 non-obvious footgun (in scope). Owner/releasers trusted; no theft, no unbacked phUSD. Surface with safe-config guidance (revoke releasers to actually freeze custody during a pause).
keep.disposition: KEEP — qa-bundle candidate Low; surface for owner triage with safe-config guidance.

This is an in-contract defense-in-depth assertion gap, latent only under a non-default setMinter repoint to a minter that does not replicate NFTMinterV2's measured-delta discipline. It is NOT the owner-driven-attack/malicious-token OOS (KI-1/KI-2) and not the external-backing model (DEDUP-001). Law-3 borderline footgun surfaced honestly at QA: a competent owner could assume this dispatcher self-defends the backing invariant like its near-identical sibling and reuse it in a new wiring.
